\newcommand{\BenchAmendmentFiveDisclosures}{Prior to confirmatory S3 execution, Amendment~5 (\texttt{17de6626}, 2026-11-23) refined S2--S5 handling from disjoint development evidence (183/183 confirmatory S2 preprocessing passes under GCC~\BenchGCC{} and 3/5 fixture-authoring stops in a 5-pair quarantined diagnostic): (i)~an S1 pass failing constructive fixture verification before S3 receives terminal \texttt{fixture\_stop} with a bucket, reason, and SHA-256-pinned proof, staying in post-S0 denominators as not executed in P1 and S9, keeping $\text{desk stop}=0$ and $\text{executed}=0$ in P2, remaining outside P3, and reporting as S14; and (ii)~confirmatory-only quota-gated execution runs the 183 confirmatory S1 passes in frozen hash order across waves (target $\le 75\%$, hard cap $80\%$ weekly quota) while recording the 204 quarantined S12 passes and any unattempted confirmatory tail as \texttt{not\_executed}. Under protocol Section~11, Wave~1--3 operational disclosures are documented alongside sensitivity toggles: \texttt{gate1\_sandbox.py} enforces \texttt{prlimit --cpu=8:8}, emitting \texttt{SIGKILL} (exit~137) rather than \texttt{SIGXCPU}; Wave~2's two 8\,s CPU kills (\texttt{oom\_kill = 0}) halted at \texttt{terminal = None} until \texttt{expansion\_run.py} was patched (\texttt{04f1a1b2}; Wave~1 baseline \texttt{1c926287} replayed identically with zero exit-137 rows) to record non-OOM exit~137/$-9$ at \texttt{cpu.stat.usage\_usec} $\ge 8\times 10^{6}$ as right-censored \texttt{cpu\_cap} and emit \texttt{insufficient\_fit} when $<4$ uncapped sizes remain. Both Wave~2 pairs re-executed to admissible \texttt{no\_alert} fits (20 and 4 \texttt{cpu\_cap} events; treating both as infrastructure failure yields P1 147/476 = 30.9\% (95\% CP 26.8--35.2\%), P2 +30.7~pp, P3 6/122 = 4.9\% (95\% CP 1.8--10.4\%)). Across all waves, \texttt{cpu\_cap} fired 28 times across 3 positions: 24 on those two Wave~2 pairs plus 4 on Wave~3 position~139 (\texttt{no\_alert}; rollback shifts P1 from 149 to 148 and leaves P3 at 6, bounding unpatched P1 at 146/476 = 30.7\% (95\% CP 26.6--35.0\%) and P3 at 6/121 = 5.0\% (95\% CP 1.8--10.5\%)). Five \texttt{raw\_terminal\_null} runs were resolved via central overlay \texttt{b598ea21} (3 in Wave~2, 2 in Wave~3): two Wave~2 pairs crashed only under UBSan (\texttt{rc = 139}) from Gate~1's 8\,MB \texttt{RLIMIT\_STACK} overhead and were classified as \texttt{execution\_infrastructure\_failure} (as \texttt{fixture\_stop}: P1--P3 unchanged, Sec.~S14 34/183); one Wave~2 overlay pair (alongside one pre-overlay Wave~1 pair, forming a 2-pair \texttt{stderr} sensitivity toggle) wrote timing to \texttt{stderr} with oracle-matching \texttt{stdout} and was recorded as \texttt{fixture\_stop} (counting both \texttt{stderr} pairs as executed: P1 151/476 = 31.7\% (95\% CP 27.6--36.1\%), P2 +29.8~pp, Sec.~S14 30/183); and two Wave~3 UB/assertion pairs (\texttt{rc = 134}) were recorded as \texttt{fixture\_stop} (as infrastructure: P1--P3 unchanged, Sec.~S14 30/183). Wave~3 also logged one capped-quality sensitivity pair (P3 6/123 = 4.9\% (95\% CP 1.8--10.3\%) if \texttt{insufficient\_fit}) and 6 SPEC-quoting \texttt{alignment\_boundary} stops (unverified by per-step timestamp). Coordinator audits restored 6 Wave~1 \texttt{execution\_oracle\_failure} terminals from worker \texttt{fixture\_stop} proposals (plus 5 pre-run non-geometric ladder fixes) and rebuilt 4 Wave~2 precision-only \texttt{alignment\_boundary} stops that executed to \texttt{execution\_oracle\_failure}, accounting for 10/17 (58.8\%) of Sec.~S4 oracle failures; counting Wave~1's 6 restored failures as \texttt{fixture\_stop} yields P1 143/476 = 30.0\% (95\% CP 26.0--34.4\%), P2 +31.5~pp (95\% bootstrap +23.3 to +39.7~pp), Sec.~S4 11/143 = 7.7\% (95\% CP 3.9--13.3\%), and Sec.~S14 38/183 = 20.8\% (95\% CP 15.1--27.4\%) (143/183 = 78.1\% (95\% CP 71.4--83.9\%) conditional yield), while treating all 10 coordinator-audited oracle failures jointly as \texttt{fixture\_stop} yields P1 139/476 = 29.2\% (95\% CP 25.2--33.5\%), Sec.~S4 7/139 = 5.0\% (95\% CP 2.0--10.1\%), and Sec.~S14 42/183 = 23.0\% (95\% CP 17.1--29.7\%). Four S1 passes (4/183) stopped in \texttt{fixture\_stop} with \texttt{original\_compile\_failure} despite passing Stage~S2 single-TU preprocessing (Sec.~S3 0/183 = 0.0\% (95\% CP 0.0--2.0\%); 0/154 = 0.0\%, $p = 4.25 \times 10^{-42}$ across the 154 S1 passes entering \texttt{expansion\_run.py} after 29 pre-runner \texttt{fixture\_stop}s and before 3 overlay \texttt{fixture\_stop} reclassifications). Pre-analysis ledger \texttt{59dcfaf3} and representative plan \texttt{99c0b425} were SHA-256-locked before computing P1--P3.}

\newcommand{\BenchAlertTableCaption}{Ordinal-indexed forensics for all 6 confirmatory all-stream alerts (positions in frozen 1--183 confirmatory hash order; all 6/6 passed $\ge 80\%$ causal restoration). ``str.'' gives distinct $(n, T(n), Q(n))$ trajectories across the 3 streams. Positions~13 and~164 have constant reference $c_0$; Position~164 is strictly event-scoped ($c_0$ slope 1.00 vs.\ combined $c_0{+}c_1$ slope 0.00 and $2.00\times$ total-tick ratio because auxiliary $c_1$ performs identical linear work on both sides). Position~3 exhibits low log-linear fit quality ($R^2_{\min} = 0.061$) and flips to \texttt{no\_alert} on drop-largest refit; under a descriptive post-hoc diagnostic filter requiring primary $c_0$, total-tick $c_0{+}c_1$, $R^2 \ge 0.94$, drop-largest retention, and $\ge 80\%$ restoration simultaneously, 4/124 (3.2\%) fits remain (Positions~13, 94, 97, and~175). Single-process \texttt{plain} CPU ratios include $\approx 15$--$22$\,ms sandbox startup overhead, masking sub-millisecond workloads on Positions~3, 94, and~97.}
\newcommand{\BenchStreamAndFitForensics}{Across all 124 admitted fits, 70/124 (56.5\%) produced 3/3 distinct $(n, T(n), Q(n))$ stream trajectories, 9/124 (7.3\%) produced 2/3, and 45/124 (36.3\%) had input-value-invariant counts identical across all 3 streams (3/6 distinct vs.\ 3/6 size-determined among alerts). Log-ratio $R^2$ across the 18 alerting streams had median 0.9999 (range 0.061--1.0000, with $R^2 \ge 0.946$ on all 15 streams outside Position~3), whereas across all 372 fitted streams 171 had exact zero log-ratio variance and the remaining 201 had median $R^2 = 0.864$. Drop-largest refit admissibility held for both outcomes: 6/6 alerts (5 retained, 1 flipped) and 117/118 (99.2\%) non-alerts (117 remained \texttt{no\_alert}, 0 flipped, 1 range-limited).}
\newcommand{\BenchBaselineScreens}{Evaluating alternative baseline screens on the same 124 admitted fits quantifies each safeguard's selectivity: (i)~a largest-size ratio-only screen ($T/Q \ge 1.50$ on all streams, no slope cutoff) alerts on 32/124 = 25.8\% (95\% CP 18.4--34.4\%), admitting 26 non-alerts failing the all-stream slope floor (12 flat $|\text{slope}| \le 0.05$ constant-factor ratios, 6 positive sub-0.50 slopes, 5 negative-slope precomputation cases whose ratio shrinks with $n$, and 3 stream-selective Sec.~S7 cases; $5.3\times$ over-alerting); (ii)~a slope-only screen ($\ge 0.50$, no ratio floor) yields 7/124 = 5.6\% (95\% CP 2.3--11.3\%) (1 sub-$1.50\times$ case); (iii)~requiring dual-cutoff growth on combined primary-plus-auxiliary total ticks ($c_0{+}c_1$) yields 5/124 = 4.0\% (95\% CP 1.3--9.2\%) (5 of 6 primary alerts retained, 0 additional alerts, filtering event-scoped Position~164); and (iv)~naive single-process \texttt{plain} CPU-time screens (\texttt{cpu.stat.usage\_usec} at $\ge 10$\,ms) yield 0/124 = 0.0\% (95\% CP 0.0--2.9\%) under the 4-size dual rule (process-startup overhead flattens small-$n$ slopes) and 17/124 = 13.7\% (95\% CP 8.2--21.0\%) under largest-size CPU ratio $\ge 1.50$ (recovering 3/6 primary alerts---Positions~13, 164, and~175---while flagging 14 non-alerts failing the all-stream logical-slope screen). Under a descriptive post-hoc diagnostic filter combining total-tick growth, drop-largest retention, $R^2 \ge 0.94$, and $\ge 80\%$ restoration, 4/124 = 3.2\% (95\% CP 0.9--8.1\%) remain (Positions~13, 94, 97, and~175).}
\newcommand{\BenchAuthorConfusionProse}{Across the three non-empty primary buckets, the primary rater's 22 \texttt{pass} decisions split under blind author review into 3 \texttt{pass}, 12 \texttt{contract} stops, and 7 \texttt{source} stops; its 26 \texttt{contract} stops split into 19 \texttt{contract}, 3 \texttt{pass}, and 4 \texttt{source}; and both \texttt{source} stops agreed (2/2). Disagreement stemmed predominantly from stricter author screening on contract and source eligibility rather than arbitrary noise, alongside the 32/183 = 17.5\% (95\% CP 12.3--23.8\%) constructive pre-S3 \texttt{fixture\_stop} rate.}
\newcommand{\BenchAuthorDownstream}{Stratifying the 50-pair blind draw by cohort (20 confirmatory, 30 quarantined) reveals both directions of the S1 disagreement: of the 9 confirmatory pairs rated \texttt{pass} by primary S1 (all 9 cluster representatives), the 1 author-\texttt{pass} pair executed to \texttt{no\_alert}, all 3 author-\texttt{contract}-stop pairs executed to \texttt{no\_alert}, and the 5 author-\texttt{source}-stop pairs ended at 1 \texttt{fixture\_stop}, 1 \texttt{insufficient\_fit}, and 3 \texttt{no\_alert}---so 7/8 (87.5\%) author-rejected S1 passes constructively cleared fixture authoring, optimization/sham invariance, and Gate~1 execution with 0/8 false growth alerts, whereas 3/26 (11.5\%) sampled workflow \texttt{contract} stops were rated \texttt{pass} by the blind author and remain unexecuted in P1/P2/Sec.~S13.}
\newcommand{\BenchDiscussionSynthesis}{Comparing P2 across all 476 post-intake clusters (+30.3~pp, Holm $p = 6.78 \times 10^{-12}$) against Sec.~S13 excluding the 118 held \texttt{desk\_unrateable} clusters (+7.3~pp across 358 rateable Contest clusters, 95\% cluster bootstrap $-2.8$ to +17.0~pp, nominal exact sign-flip $p = 0.165$ outside the primary Holm family) shows that overall desk-stop dominance is driven by missing self-contained specifications (86 unbundled contest-image clusters and all 32 Repository clusters lacking an independent spec), whereas among rateable Contest clusters desk stops (48.9\%) and isolated execution (41.6\%) occur at comparable scales; across completed observations, count invariance held with zero disagreements across optimization levels (9{,}794 \texttt{-O0}/\texttt{-O2}/\texttt{-O3} agreements, 0 disagreements, 1{,}294 capped or missing) and sham edits (7{,}349 target--sham agreements, 0 disagreements, 967 capped or missing), and all 6 all-stream alerts (6/6) passed $\ge 80\%$ causal restoration (0 failed), yet fitted-case all-stream alerts remained rare (6/124 = 4.8\% (95\% CP 1.8--10.2\%)).}
